d: Qiddiya Investment Company (QIC), a PIF-backed giga project, is central to Saudi Vision 2030’s goal of building a vibrant society, thriving economy, and ambitious nation. By harnessing the power of Play, QIC brings entertainment, sports, and culture to the forefront in Qiddiya City—a futuristic destination featuring world-class attractions, sports complexes, cultural landmarks, and residential neighborhoods.

Act as the CCU’s working-level liaison officer with Ministry of Interior agencies, Public Security, Civil Defence, Qiddiya Police, the Patrol Dispatch Centre and the Principality of Riyadh Province, maintaining current contacts, coordination matrices and escalation routes under the Joint Security Operating Model (JSOM).

Coordinate the government approvals, permits, inspections and completion certificates required for events, openings, drone operations, fireworks and other regulated activities, tracking each to completion with venue and project teams.

Support the joint coordination arrangements – liaison-officer frameworks, information-sharing protocols, joint meetings, workshops and exercises with the authorities – including preparation of agendas, briefs and records.
Prepare and translate correspondence, briefings, reports and presentations in Arabic and English for government stakeholders, ensuring accuracy, protocol and tone.
Support the dissemination and upkeep of the JSOM across Ministry of Interior sub-departments, including workshops and the maintenance of names, roles and contact details.
Coordinate official visits, delegations and inspections to the CCU and Qiddiya assets with Security, Event Management and the venues.
Maintain the register of government engagements, commitments, actions and reporting obligations, including reporting to the Principality and shareholder requirements, and ensure follow-through.
Provide liaison support during incidents and heightened alert states, relaying information between the CCU and the authorities and recording decisions.
Support drone-governance interfaces with the authorities alongside the Manager – Airspace.
Maintain the authority contact directory and liaison-officer roster, with periodic verification.
Log and track permit and approval applications, with status reporting to the Assistant Manager – Security and the CCU.
Produce bilingual briefing notes, letters and minutes to QIC standards.
Support the Alert State process and national alert notifications within the CCU.
Support government-facing exercises, drills and familiarisation visits, including Civil Defence site familiarisation.
Maintain protocol guidance for hosting government officials at Qiddiya.
Contribute to planning, reporting and continual improvement within the function.
Support and share knowledge with colleagues, operators and client teams.
Promote a culture of accountability, safety and continual improvement.
Maintain accurate records and provide timely reports and recommendations to the line manager.
Perform other related duties consistent with the role and business requirements, including support to incidents, exercises and events outside normal hours.
q: Bachelor’s degree in Security Studies, Public Administration, Law, Political Science, International Relations or a closely related discipline.
Security, emergency-management or protocol certification is desirable.
Professional translation or official-correspondence training is an advantage.
Native-level Arabic and fluent English, written and spoken, with strong formal-correspondence and translation skills.
Strong knowledge of Saudi government structures, Ministry of Interior agencies, permit and approval processes and official protocol.
Strong stakeholder-management, discretion and relationship-building skills.
Strong organisation, record-keeping and follow-up discipline.
Ability to work calmly in a 24/7 operational environment and during incidents.
Minimum 3 years of relevant experience in government relations, security liaison, public-sector coordination or protocol, ideally within a giga-project, major venue or government-related entity.
Experience supporting security or emergency-services coordination is preferred.
Demonstrated experience liaising with Saudi government and security authorities.
Experience managing permits, approvals and inspections for events or operational assets.
Saudi national strongly preferred, given the government-liaison nature of the role.
